property_summary: After any sequence of addToBalance and withdrawBalance operations, the contract's ETH balance equals the sum of user balances
After two addToBalance calls from distinct users, the contract ETH balance equals the sum of their balances.
After two addToBalance calls from distinct users without withdrawals, the contract ETH balance equals the sum of their balances.
After two addToBalance calls from distinct users without withdrawals, the contract ETH balance equals the sum of their balances.
After two addToBalance calls from distinct users without withdrawals, the contract ETH balance equals the sum of their balances, provided no overflow occurs in the additions.

After any sequence of addToBalance calls, the sum of all user balances must equal the total ether deposited; the bug breaks this by overwriting balance to msg.value, causing the invariant to fail when more than one deposit is made to the same address.
After two deposits from the same address, the user's balance must be the sum of the two amounts; the bug sets the balance to the second amount alone.

After any sequence of addToBalance calls (including zero-value calls), the balance of any address that has never called addToBalance must remain zero; the bug incorrectly sets the caller's balance to msg.value when msg.value equals zero, overwriting the previous balance.

After any deposit via addToBalance, the caller's balance must be at least the sent msg.value; the buggy version overwrites the balance to msg.value, so if a previous withdrawal left userBalance[caller] at 0, a subsequent deposit with msg.value > 0 satisfies the invariant in both versions, but if a deposited amount is greater than the sent msg.value due to a prior non-zero balance, the invariant can still hold — the actual violation is that after two deposits from the same address, the final balance equals the last msg.value instead of the sum, so the invariant 'balance >= last deposit amount' still holds, but the stronger invariant 'balance equals cumulative deposits' is broken; specifically, after any sequence of addToBalance calls, the sum of all user balances must equal the total Ether deposited into the contract; the bug breaks this because it overwrites the balance to msg.value, discarding previous deposits.
After addToBalance sends ETH, the contract's balance must increase by the sent amount.
